items.question: What practice must follow worship of this circle to produce its effects?
premises: The application continues for a duration
items.inference: Sustained meditation after worship activates the circle's power.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped this circle, one should apply meditation for as long as one continues the practice.

items.question: What kinds of languages become perceptible through this meditative practice?
items.inference: The practice grants access to diverse languages, both familiar and unfamiliar.
uncertainties: Agreement between feminine bhāṣās and neuter aśrutāni/śrutāni is taken as describing the languages.
items.plain_english: Indeed, languages of various forms, both unheard and heard, become manifest.

items.question: Where and by whom are these languages heard in the yogic experience?
items.inference: The perception of languages is entirely internal and self-contained.
items.plain_english: By oneself alone, they are heard by oneself, for oneself, and within oneself.

items.question: What bodily transformation results from the successful practice of this circle?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair
The practitioner resembles the god of love
This resemblance is as a second Kāma
items.inference: The practice confers youthful beauty comparable to Kāma.
items.plain_english: Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, one becomes like a second god of love.

rows.grounds: object or source to be destroyed

items.question: What effect does destroying the power of wind and related forces have on speech?
premises: The power of wind and others is destroyed by speech
The person stands like a mute
items.inference: Neutralizing these forces through speech renders one silent like a mute.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation of vāyvādeḥ and vācā is somewhat ambiguous.
items.plain_english: One should destroy the force of wind and the rest by speech; then he indeed stands like a mute.

items.question: What supreme power is attributed to the seventh circle addressed to the goddess?
premises: It is addressed to the goddess
It is described as supreme and army-paralyzing
items.inference: The seventh circle possesses the supreme power to paralyze armies.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the seventh circle is supreme and causes the paralysis of armies.

items.question: What perceptual ability arises for one devoted to worship and meditation on this circle?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to worship and meditation
items.inference: Devotion to this circle grants the ability to see from a distance.
items.plain_english: And for one devoted to worship and meditation on that circle, vision arises from afar.

items.question: What additional magical powers are accomplished through this circle's practice?
premises: Paralyzing, deluding, and similar acts are mentioned
These are addressed to the beloved goddess
items.inference: The practice enables killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and related powers.
items.plain_english: O fortunate one, O beloved, killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and such powers are attained.

items.question: What knowledge is required for success in these ritual methods?
premises: The method of eight times eight must be known
items.inference: Knowledge of the eightfold-eight method is necessary for success.
items.plain_english: Having known the method of the eight groups of eight, one succeeds; not otherwise.

items.question: How should the teaching declared here be ascertained with certainty?
premises: The teaching is declared without doubt by me
Devotion and reasoning are the means
items.inference: The teaching must be firmly ascertained through both devotion and reasoning.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of avadhāram as object of an implied action is inferred.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this has been declared by me without doubt; ascertain it with devotion and reasoning.

premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
items.inference: This marks the end of the eighth chapter in the Candradvīpa text.
items.plain_english: In the work emerged from Candradvīpa, this is the eighth chapter.

items.question: What teaching does the speaker promise to explain to the beloved?
premises: The speaker promises to tell something
The topic is the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs
items.inference: The speaker will explain the arrangement of the yoginī rows.
items.plain_english: O beloved, I shall tell you the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.

items.question: What collective group encompasses all earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs?
items.inference: All earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs together constitute the complete field-group.
items.plain_english: This is the complete field-group of all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.

items.question: Which categories of yoginīs are included in this comprehensive enumeration?
items.inference: The enumeration comprises innate, family-born, and door-guardian yoginīs.
uncertainties: sarvakulajā appears in singular-like form but is read as plural in this list.
items.plain_english: All the innate ones, all those born of the families, and all the door-guardians.

items.question: Why has the supreme secret among secrets been revealed now?
premises: It is the supreme secret among secrets
The revelation is due to your devotion
items.inference: The supreme secret is revealed because of the devotee's devotion.
items.plain_english: The supreme secret of secrets has been revealed because of your devotion.

items.question: What instruction does the speaker now wish to hear from the gurus?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The wish is to hear something
The topic is the worship of the siddhas from the gurus
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear about the worship of the siddhas from the gurus.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.

items.question: To whom should the arrangement of the two syllables be imparted?
premises: An arrangement of two syllables is specified
items.inference: The two-syllable arrangement should be imparted to others as appropriate.
uncertainties: The precise meaning of anyanteṣu in this context is unclear.
items.plain_english: One should impart the arrangement of the two syllables to others.

items.question: What claim is made about the uniqueness of this knowledge across time?
premises: No knowledge equal to this exists again
No knowledge equal to this will exist in the future
The comparison is made with this knowledge
items.inference: This knowledge is unparalleled in past and future.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there ever be again.

items.question: What does the speaker promise to explain to the beautiful-eyed listener?
premises: The topic is the method of their names
items.inference: The speaker will explain the method of their names.
items.plain_english: I shall speak the method of their names; listen, O beautiful-eyed one.

items.question: How are the independent impellers of the family identified in this teaching?
premises: The term caturyuga is used as a designation
They are addressed in relation to the lord
They are independent impellers of the family
items.inference: The independent impellers of the family are designated as caturyuga.

items.plain_english: O Lord, they are called the four ages, the independent impellers of the family.

items.question: What is the extent and origin attributed to this Kaula teaching?
items.inference: The Kaula teaching is vast in extent and of supreme origin.
uncertainties: The exact sense of daśakoṭipramāṇaṃ (verses, mantras, or extent) is unclear.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, measures ten crores.

items.question: By what agency and will does the yoginī named Icchā extend up to Māyā?
premises: The extent reaches up to Māyā by supreme will
items.inference: The yoginī Icchā, through the siddhas and by supreme will, extends up to Māyā.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation between siddhaiḥ and māyāntaṃ is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, by the siddhas and by supreme will, extends up to Māyā.

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching concerning the Mothers to the goddess?
premises: The sky-movers are the agents of transmission
items.inference: The sky-movers transmitted the teaching concerning the Mothers.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, O beloved, it was told again concerning the Mothers by the sky-movers.

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching concerning the earth-moving yoginīs who are good eaters?
premises: The subject concerns the earth-moving yoginīs

items.plain_english: O beloved, it was told concerning the earth-moving, good-eating yoginīs by an earth-mover.
